card.name: Modifier word before a noun in set phrases
card.fires_on: A short modifier such as patient, human, your, our or safety, placed right before a noun in a stock phrase. It is most common in label phrases like "individual patient treatment goals" and "no available human data".

modes.label: Individual patient
modes.description: The word patient after "consistent with individual" in the NSAID dosing sentence.
modes.example: Use the lowest effective dosage for the shortest duration consistent with individual<< patient>> treatment goals [see WARNINGS AND PRE

modes.label: Human data
modes.description: The word human before data in pregnancy and animal-study sections.
modes.example: There are no available<< human>> data to assess for any drug associated risks

modes.label: Possessive in general text
modes.description: A possessive such as our or your before a noun in ordinary prose.
modes.example: listening to<< your>> body and backing off when necessary.

card.writes: It promotes words like twice and tolerance and suppresses opinion words, so the effect is unclear.
card.plain: It marks a small modifier word that sits just before the noun in a fixed phrase, like "individual patient" or "human data".
